name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,584

clue.text: Bloomer from servant in base with Poles touring States

indicators.note: the servant is placed within the word for base, which wraps around it
to tour is to travel all round something, so the Poles go around the States

blocks.note: a bed is a base or foundation, as in a bed of gravel
a lackey is a footman or servant
S and N are the south and north poles
the United States

explanation.surface: A flower comes from a servant at a military base where Polish visitors are touring America.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloomer looks like a blunder or an item of underwear, but here it is a thing that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: The black-eyed Susan is a yellow daisy-like garden plant with a dark centre, so it is a flowering thing.

clue.text: This as basis for the annual blow-out?

definitions.text: This as basis for the annual blow-out?

blocks.note: surface reading: a big yearly party or feast that something forms the foundation of
setter's reading: the yearly occasion when candles are literally blown out, and this item holds them

explanation.walkthrough: A blow-out is slang for a lavish party, but read literally it is the blowing out of candles once a year.
explanation.definitionFit: The cake baked for someone's anniversary of being born carries the candles that get extinguished in one breath.

clue.text: Very quietly brought into AA, left in dismay

indicators.note: being brought into something means going inside it, so the quiet sign sits within the pair of letters

blocks.note: taken as written
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quietly
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone is quietly taken into Alcoholics Anonymous and then left feeling dismayed.
explanation.walkthrough: AA suggests Alcoholics Anonymous or the motoring organisation, but here it is just two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal someone is to fill them with horror and shock, which is what dismaying them does.

clue.text: Venomous type, man attracting firm support

blocks.note: a king is a man, or piece, in chess
Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A spiteful sort of man draws in a company's backing.
explanation.walkthrough: Man as a chess piece is a crossword convention, and the word KING comes from it.
explanation.definitionFit: The king cobra is the world's longest poisonous snake, an example of a creature with toxic bite.

clue.text: Any degenerates get involved with Zulu banker?

indicators.note: something that degenerates falls apart and loses its form, so the letters of any are scrambled
involved means tangled up, so get is mixed in with the rest

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
Zulu is Z in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A worried question about any declining banker getting mixed up with a Zulu.
explanation.walkthrough: A banker is crossword shorthand for a river, something that has banks, not a financier.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yangtze is China's longest river, and rivers flow between banks, hence the crossword-only sense.

clue.text: Cold as princess taken with street worker

blocks.note: Di, the late Princess of Wales
St is the abbreviation for street
a worker ant; ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A princess turns frosty when seen in the company of a road sweeper.
explanation.definitionFit: Distant describes someone aloof and unfriendly in manner, the same chilly reserve as cold.

clue.text: Main threat stole lead from trader with uranium

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its front, so only its opening letter is wanted

blocks.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium
a boa is a feathery or fur stole worn round the neck
the first letter of trader

explanation.surface: A thief threatening the high street: someone stole a merchant's lead, along with some uranium.
explanation.walkthrough: Stole looks like a verb about theft, but it is the noun for a scarf. The main is the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A German submarine menaced Allied shipping on the high seas, so it was a danger on the ocean.

clue.text: The claims that could be made by such as Paracelsus

indicators.note: something that could be made from these letters is a new word built by rearranging them

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The bold assertions a Renaissance figure like Paracelsus might put forward.
explanation.walkthrough: Paracelsus was a 16th-century Swiss physician famous for his work on transmuting metals and elixirs.
explanation.definitionFit: Paracelsus practised the medieval proto-chemistry of turning base metals to gold, so he is one example.

clue.text: Epitaph for cricket side in Harrogate location?

blocks.note: RIP, rest in peace, is the standard gravestone inscription
the on side is one half of a cricket field, also called leg side

explanation.surface: A gravestone inscription for a cricket team from somewhere around Harrogate.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrogate is a spa town in North Yorkshire; the question mark admits the place is near it rather than in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripon is a small cathedral city a few miles north of the town, part of the same borough area.

clue.text: Pretty good UN school assembly

indicators.note: an assembly puts parts together into a new arrangement, so these letters are rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A school run by the United Nations holds a rather impressive morning gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: Assembly looks like a school's morning meeting, which suits the surface perfectly.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone no slouch is an idiom meaning they are quite capable, accomplished or skilled.

clue.text: Doctor has pie prepared as medical speciality

indicators.note: food that is prepared is cut up and reworked, so the letters are made into something new

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A physician serves up a pie that turns out to be his specialist field.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor looks like the anagram signal, as it often is, but here it is part of the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Orthopaedics is the branch of surgery dealing with bones, joints and muscles, one field of hospital practice.

clue.text: Mistakenly call the malignant hag

indicators.note: doing something mistakenly means getting it wrong, so the letters come out in the wrong order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wrongly names the wicked old woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A hellcat is a spiteful, furious woman, often a witch-like figure of fury and bad temper.

clue.text: Nocturnal creature needs attention following an illness

indicators.note: following places one part after the other, so the attention piece comes at the end

blocks.note: taken as written
TB, tuberculosis, is an illness
to give someone your ear is to pay them attention

explanation.surface: An animal of the night needs looking after once it has fallen ill.
explanation.definitionFit: The ant bear, or aardvark, is an African burrowing mammal that feeds on termites after dark.

clue.text: Improvised German newspaper article sent over

indicators.note: sending something over flips it, so the words are read from the end back

blocks.note: Bild is a German tabloid daily
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A German paper hastily throws together a piece and sends it abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Bild is Germany's best-selling tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: To ad-lib is to speak or perform without preparation, so something improvised is ad-libbed off the cuff.

clue.text: Yearns to have house on or very close to sea

blocks.note: to long is to yearn
ho. is the abbreviation for house
re means on or about, regarding

explanation.surface: Someone longs for a home right beside the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Longshore describes things found along or near the coast, as in longshore drift on beaches.

clue.text: Found priest quiet, nursing wound

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold something close in your arms, so the priest holds the wound inside

blocks.note: Eli is the Old Testament priest who raised Samuel
a stab is a wound made with a blade
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A priest was found quietly tending a stab wound.
explanation.walkthrough: Found looks like the past of find, but it is the verb meaning to set up.
explanation.definitionFit: To found an institution is to set it up or create it, the same as to establish it.

clue.text: Bachelor, single friend, providing skeleton service?

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in BA
one is a single
china is rhyming slang: china plate means mate

explanation.surface: An unmarried man and a pal lay on only a bare-bones operation.
explanation.walkthrough: China for friend is Cockney rhyming slang, from china plate rhyming with mate. Service here means a set of crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: This fine porcelain contains ground animal ash, so a dinner set of it is literally made with skeleton.

clue.text: Can it go on spreading?

indicators.note: spreading scatters things about, so the words before it are dispersed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A worried question about whether something will keep on spreading.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description: the fear about an epidemic is whether it will continue to pass on.
explanation.definitionFit: Contagion is the transmission of disease between people, the very thing that worries everyone by passing on.

clue.text: National Prime Minister twice having day out

indicators.note: having something out means it has gone, so the letter for day is dropped

blocks.note: Benjamin Disraeli served two terms as British prime minister
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: A two-term premier takes a day off.
explanation.walkthrough: Twice is not a repeat instruction; it identifies the premier who held office in 1868 and again in 1874-80.
explanation.definitionFit: A national is a citizen of a country, and an Israeli is a citizen of Israel.

clue.text: Nothing venerable arising from Las Vegas?

indicators.note: in a down entry, arising means going upward, so the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: nada is Spanish for nothing
Ven. is the abbreviation for venerable, a title for an archdeacon

explanation.surface: Nothing respectable ever comes out of Las Vegas.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows the definition is by example: Las Vegas is one city in the state.
explanation.definitionFit: Las Vegas lies in Nevada, so a person or thing belonging there is a native of that state.

clue.text: Tennis call Don overturned

indicators.note: overturning flips something over, so the word for don is read backwards

blocks.note: to don clothes is to put them on

explanation.surface: A tennis umpire's call has been overruled by a university fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: Don looks like a university lecturer, but here it is the verb for getting dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis an umpire shouts this when a ball bounces twice before the player reaches it.

clue.text: Material broadcast in disputed region

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard over the airwaves, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: cashmere is a fine wool fabric

explanation.surface: Fabric is shown on television in a contested territory.
explanation.walkthrough: The wool takes its name from the goats of this very region.
explanation.definitionFit: Kashmir is a Himalayan territory whose ownership has long been contested by India and Pakistan.

clue.text: African male in perfect health ingests arsenic

indicators.note: to ingest is to swallow, so the arsenic symbol goes inside

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for male
As is the chemical symbol for arsenic
A1 means first-rate, with the digit read as the letter I

explanation.surface: An African man in fine fettle swallows poison.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 in perfect health becomes AI with the one read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Masai are a pastoral people of Kenya and Tanzania, so a member is an African.

clue.text: Noble having sex with French philosopher

blocks.note: sex is Latin for six, which is VI in Roman numerals
Auguste Comte was the French founder of positivism

explanation.surface: An aristocrat is having an affair with a French thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: Sex is not about intimacy here: it is the Latin word for six.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicomte is a French viscount, a member of the titled aristocracy ranking below a count.

clue.text: The London Eye?

blocks.note: surface reading: the giant observation wheel on the South Bank of the Thames
setter's reading: what a Londoner using Cockney rhyming slang calls an eye

explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang mince pies means eyes, often shortened to just the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockneys, the traditional East End speakers, say mince pies for eyes and then drop the rhyming part.

clue.text: He has dog rolling barrel

indicators.note: rolling tumbles things over and over, so the letters land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man's dog is rolling a barrel along.
explanation.definitionFit: A hogshead is a large cask for wine or beer, traditionally holding about 54 imperial gallons.

clue.text: Rasta unity also seen in Independent twice

indicators.note: being seen in something means sitting inside it, so the word for also goes between

blocks.note: I is the abbreviation for independent, taken two times
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: Rastafarian oneness also appears twice in a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: Independent suggests the newspaper running this puzzle, but it is just its abbreviation, I.
explanation.definitionFit: Rastafarians use this phrase for we, expressing the oneness of every person with God and each other.

clue.text: Business leaders sincere: mikados corrupt

indicators.note: corrupt means spoilt or altered from the proper state, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Executives claim to be honest, while Japanese emperors are crooked.
explanation.walkthrough: A mikado is a title for the emperor of Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: Executives in charge of companies are the people who make the key choices, hence the phrase.
